Every operation declares an explicit cause and the write permit derives from that cause alone, never from measurement success or serialized inequality: qualifying mode choices, terminal moved gestures and the three reset branches keep their exactly-once persist, while pointer previews, no-move/return-to-start/pointercancel rollback, adoption, render reconciliation, refit, refresh, window resize, scroll and teardown never write. The six independent this.persist() handler call sites in src/muya/lib/tableResize/index.js (lines ~1486 mode choice, ~1925 wall drag terminal, ~1947 column drag terminal, ~1994 wall reset, ~2030 whole-table column reset, ~2057 partial column reset) collapse into one authorized completion call site. Pure fit maths, entry identity, schema v2, the serializer, the rememberTableColumnSizes persist gate and all lifecycle fences are preserved; tableFit.js, tableCue.js, the renderer store/profile schema, preferences, CSS/template literals, render/index.js and eventHandler/resize.js stay byte-identical.

T-001.Title: Completion stage in tableResize; the six persist call sites replaced

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/muya/lib/tableResize/index.js gains one internal completion stage completeTableOperation(cause, context) owning the final sequence positionTableWalls + ensureColumnWalls, syncTableCue, owned-repaint bookkeeping and the authorized persist; an explicit COMPLETION_CAUSE enum covers mode choice, wall/column drag end, wall reset, column reset, gesture rollback, preview, adopt, reconcile, refit, refresh, window, scroll and destroy, and the write permit is the static per-cause set only. The six persist call sites at ~1486 (setModeFromElement), ~1925 (wall drag terminal), ~1947 (column drag terminal), ~1994 (wall reset), ~2030 (whole-table column reset) and ~2057 (partial column reset) each end in one stage call; handlers no longer independently assemble the walls/cue/persist tail. No-move/return-to-start rollback tails keep their current moved predicates verbatim and never write; pointercancel keeps sharing handlePointerUp with pointerup and no new cancel policy appears. Read-only funnels (reconcileAfterRender, refitNow/refitAll, refreshTableSurfaces, handleScrollCapture, handleWindowResize, applyPersistedLayouts and the generation-fenced delayed adoption) route their tails through the stage with non-writing causes. Hidden/zero-geometry mode choices still persist their mode intent and retry layout on a later measurable pass without a second write. persist() internals are untouched: rememberTableColumnSizes gate, syncIdentities({ adoptPersisted: false }) before serialization, this.persisted replaced before the single muya-table-layouts dispatch. tableFit.js, tableCue.js, render/index.js, eventHandler/resize.js, CSS/template literals, schema and preferences stay byte-identical.

The suite characterizes the cause/readiness/write matrix on the real TableResize model and DOM: mode Auto/Fit/Full including repeated choice and hidden/zero-geometry deferred layout (mode intent persisted, exactly one dispatch per qualifying action, layout retried later without a second write); wall and column pointer preview and terminal moved gestures; no-move/return-to-start/pointercancel rollback restoring the baseline; wall reset; whole-table and partial fitted reset with fit before persist. Assertions pin final widths/manual flags/ratios/mode, muya-table-layouts event counts and payload content (identities synchronized with adoptPersisted:false, this.persisted equal to the dispatched entries, remember-off skipping the dispatch) and the ABSENCE of profile writes from preview, adoption, reconcile, refit, refresh, window and scroll completions — not merely invocation of the new helper. Mutation controls detect a refresh-cause write permit (a refresh completion must not dispatch even when serialization would differ) and old-snapshot re-adoption during a user commit. Teardown assertions cover destroy() cancelling owned repaint/refit/adoption work and restoring prior transforms.
